_comment: Human layer. Overrides win over the collector, but they can never delete an
entry the collector keeps finding: use `exclude` for that, which is
deliberate and shows up in the diff.
Keys: featured (pinned and marked), category, tier, evidence, summary,
notes (a short 'reusable engineering decision'), media, exclude (list of ids).

gh:typesafe-ai/skills.notes: The vendor's own agent skills. Because it is updated continuously, it is the closest thing to a specification of how TypeSafe intends Jev to be driven from an agent.

gh:typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python.notes: Synchronous and asynchronous clients. The fastest path from an API key to a typed decision, and the reference the community clients are compared against.

gh:typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js.notes: TypeScript client where the answer type is inferred from the question you asked, so a mismatched return type is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise.

gh:typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python.notes: Drop-in replacement that backs the same interface with an ordinary LLM provider. This is the honest way to A/B a typed decision against a prompt, on your own data, before committing to either.

gh:tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction.notes: Replaces a coding agent's context-compaction summary with a typed decision. A clean example of swapping one LLM call in an existing pipeline rather than rebuilding the pipeline.

gh:TianyuCodings/NanoJev.notes: A small replica of the parallel-decision shape. Useful for reading the architecture without the vendor stack, and it is how several claims about the interface first became checkable.

gh:gargpratyush/jev-router.notes: Routes each turn to the cheapest model that can handle it. The canonical cost-reduction use case for a System One model.

gh:0xNatoshi/jev-codex-router.notes: Per-turn model and reasoning-effort routing for a coding agent, driven by typed decisions.

gh:kshetrajna12/reflex.notes: An open decision model with the same state-plus-typed-question interface. Worth reading as a shape reference even if you never run it.

gh:NiazMorshed2007/jev-review.notes: Local-first MCP plugin for continuous code review. Representative of the fastest-growing category in this list: a typed decision placed in front of an agent's next action.

gh:jkudish/jev-mcp.notes: An early proof of concept for exposing Jev over MCP, which is how most non-Python toolchains reach it.

gh:dbreunig/building-with-jev-skill.notes: A skill for writing programs that call Jev, rather than a program that calls Jev. The distinction matters: it encodes the design rules, not one implementation of them.

gh:DevMortimer/pi-warden.notes: Guardrails that steer an agent before it acts. Demonstrates the gate pattern, where the decision is cheap enough to run on every step.

gh:Dicklesworthstone/skillranker.notes: Ranks agent skills with a typed decision. A useful model for any 'choose among N candidates' problem that was previously a prompt.

gh:bnsd55/jevmlx.notes: Parallel constrained decisions on Apple Silicon via MLX. Local execution removes the per-call cost argument entirely.

gh:iammrduncan/typesafe-ai-benchmark.notes: A gateway that mimics the System One interface, which is what makes side-by-side benchmarking possible without rewriting the caller.

gh:supercorp-ai/supercov.notes: Code quality and coverage verdicts produced as typed decisions rather than prose, so the result can gate a pipeline directly.

gh:r-ms/mini-jev.notes: The most useful independent reproduction to read: it shows the read-the-logits mechanism working, and it also warns explicitly that the share it reads out is not a calibrated probability. That warning is the single most important caveat in this ecosystem.

gh:ekzhang/openjev-sglang.notes: A Jev-compatible endpoint served from open models, so the interface can be exercised without the hosted API.

gh:moritzkremb/jev-voice-browser.notes: Voice-driven browser control where the intent check is a typed decision. Shows the latency budget a gate needs to be worth running.

gh:gamesonrblx/Jevbridge.notes: Bridges the typed-decision layer to the agent protocols other tools already speak.

gh:yusukebe/hono-jev-router.notes: Semantic HTTP routing for Hono. A rare example of a typed decision used for infrastructure rather than for AI plumbing.
